text: Wolfe (Netflix) · published 9 November 2026 In one line: A long explainer of Marek and Ryabinin's score-centering paper: when rollouts come from a sampler q that differs from the trainer p, the expected policy-gradient update at each prefix splits into drift (the expected reward times the trainer's expected score under the sampler, a pull toward the sampler that ignores which rollouts won) and signal (a covariance), and subtracting that expected score, computed from the sampler's top 128 log-probabilities, cancels drift without importance ratios; the evidence is the paper's, on deliberately severe mismatch with Qwen3-0.6B on Countdown and Qwen3-30B-A3B on math, measured as training accuracy.

text: The evidence, judged . read it (38 min) · Score Centering Stabilizes Off-policy Reinforcement Learning (the paper it explains) · logs and code (martin-marek/score-centering) The idea in one sentence: when rollouts come from a sampler whose probabilities differ slightly from the trainer's, every policy-gradient update carries a hidden term, the expected reward times the trainer's expected score under the sampler, that pulls the trainer toward the sampler whatever the rewards say, and because the sampler is then refreshed from the trainer the pull compounds; subtracting that expected score from each token's score (score centering) cancels it exactly, with no importance ratios.
label: core
